content:
Step 1: Decide what you want to build

Be specific. For example:

A portfolio website
A SaaS landing page
An online store
A blog
An AI tool
A job board

The clearer your idea, the better the AI performs.

Step 2: Choose an AI coding platform

Some of the best options are:

Cursor
Claude
GitHub Copilot
https://t.co/HD9dVKAzum
Lovable
Replit

For beginners, https://t.co/HD9dVKAzum, Lovable, or Replit are the easiest.

Step 3: Give AI a detailed prompt

Instead of saying:

> Build me a website.

Say something like:

> Build a modern dark-themed landing page for my AI agency. Include a hero section, pricing cards, testimonials, FAQs, contact form, and mobile responsiveness. Use blue and purple gradients with smooth animations.

The more detailed you are, the better the result.

Step 4: Improve it section by section

-Continue prompting:
-Make the navbar sticky.
-Add animations.
-Improve the typography.
-Add a pricing calculator.
-Make it load faster.
-Optimize for SEO.
-Add dark mode.

Make it look like Apple's website.

This iterative process is what many people call "vibe coding."

Step 5: Test everything

Check that:

-Buttons work
-Forms submit
-Images load
-Mobile view looks good
-No console errors
-Ask the AI to fix anything that breaks.

Step 6: Deploy your website

Popular hosting options include:
-Vercel
-Netlify
-Cloudflare

Many AI builders can deploy with just one click.

Step 7: Connect your domain

-Buy a domain from providers like:
-Namecheap
-Cloudflare

Then point it to your hosting provider.

Learn prompting

Good prompts are a huge part of vibe coding. Examples:

"Make the design look like Stripe."
"Use glassmorphism."

"Use Tailwind CSS."

"Add Framer Motion animations."

"Generate clean, reusable React components."

"Follow accessibility best practices."

"Optimize images and page speed."

ローカル環境（特にApple Siliconなど）でLLMを運用するとき、コンテキストが長くなるにつれて推論速度が「カニの歩み」のように遅くなってしまうのが大きな悩みどころですよね。😢

この物理的な制約を、スマートなシステム設計で根本から解決する方法があるんです！✨

それが「Map-Reduce（マップ・レデュース）」パターンを取り入れたエージェント設計！

・Map（分散処理）：会話履歴を持たない「ステートレスなワーカー」にタスクを細分化して並列処理させます。ワーカーに渡すのは「タスク定義、データ、出力形式」の最小コンテキストだけにするのがポイントです。🔑
・Reduce（統合処理）：ワーカーからは文章ではなく「構造化データ（JSONなど）」を出力させ、プログラム側でデータをマージ。最後のまとめだけをLLMに依頼します。 📦

会話履歴を引きずってコンテキストを肥大化させがちなCrewAIやAutoGen、標準のLangChainは、実はローカル環境には不向きなんです。💦
状態を厳密に制御できるLangGraphや、Map-Reduce機能が内蔵されたLlamaIndexを活用するか、Pythonの `asyncio` を使って自作スクリプトを組むのが驚くほど軽量でコントロールしやすくなりますよ！

さらに、プリフィルとデコードを分担するEXOや、ローカルでの画像解析を補完するLocalEyesなどの最適化技術を組み合わせれば、ローカルLLMの性能を限界まで引き出せそうです！これぞシステム設計の妙ですね。💡

【自律学習するAIへ！強化学習で進化するコーディングエージェント「TRL×OpenEnv」の衝撃】
👉  https://t.co/2bw2c1sZCU
ただコードを真似して書くだけのAIから、自分で試行錯誤して学習する「動くAIエージェント」への大進化が始まっています！

今回の主役は、強化学習（RL）を活用してコーディングAIを賢くする最先端の訓練アプローチ。これまで主流だった「教師あり学習（SFT）」は、正解データを覚えるだけでしたが、これからは実際にコードを実行し、エラーメッセージを見て修正し、テストが通るまで自律的に挑戦して学習する仕組みに変わっていきます。まさに人間がプログラミングを学ぶプロセスと同じですね！

この革新を支えるのが、以下の強力なツールたちです！

1️⃣ TRL（Transformer Reinforcement Learning）：Hugging Faceが提供する強化学習用ライブラリで、PPOやGRPOなどのアルゴリズムを簡単に使えます。
2️⃣ OpenEnv：AIがPythonなどのコードを実際に実行できる安全な環境（サンドボックス）を用意し、AIの行動とエラーなどの結果を繋ぐ役割をします。
3️⃣ Harness：実験を管理し、AIの学習プロセスをしっかり可視化・追跡します。

特に注目したいのが、最新トレンドの「GRPO」という手法です！
これは、AIに複数のコード案を同時に作らせて、その中から一番良いものを選ぶことで、複雑な「報酬モデル」を用意しなくても効率よく学習できる優れもの。

さらに、テストが通ったらプラス、構文エラーならマイナスといった「報酬設計」を細かく行うことで、デバッグからテストまで自力でこなせる本物の「AIソフトウェアエンジニア」の誕生が現実味を帯びてきました。

コミュニティに向けてオープンソース化されているので、誰でも同じ仕組みを再現できるのが素晴らしいところ。これからのAIエージェント開発のデファクトスタンダードになりそうな予感がします！

VRの世界に本当に没入するためには、どこを向いても映像に「継ぎ目（シーム）」がないことがとても重要ですよね！
今回は、動画生成モデル「LTX2.3」をベースに、完璧な360°動画を作り出す驚きのパイプラインをご紹介します！🎉

1️⃣ **EquiRoPE (Latitude-scaled RoPE)**
360°の球体ならではの「緯度ごとの歪み」を計算して自動で補正する技術！極点や赤道付近で発生しがちだった映像の破綻をきれいに解消してくれます！

2️⃣ **Circular VAE Padding**
映像の左右の端をぐるっと円環状につなぎ合わせる処理。これで、左右の継ぎ目が完全に消え去ります！

3️⃣ **Per-step Latent Rolling**
フレームとフレームの間を滑らかにつなぎ、視点移動時の連続性をしっかりとキープしてくれます！

テキストからの動画生成はもちろん、普通の平面動画を360°空間に拡張する「VR Outpainting」にも応用できるのが本当に優秀ですね！VRコンテンツの制作コストを劇的に抑えつつ、圧倒的な没入感を実現できちゃいそうです！🚀

content:
【LLMの脳手術！活性化経路の可視化と制御技術が凄い】

大規模言語モデル（LLM）の内部で、情報がどう伝わっているかを「脳手術」のように精密に可視化・操作する最先端の技術が登場しました！🧠✨

この技術では、ローカル環境でLLMを動かすための仕組み「llama.cpp」にパッチを適用し、モデル内の層（レイヤー）ごとにどのノードが活性化（反応）したかを追跡。入力から出力までのルートを「活性化経路」として描き出します。特定のニューロンの塊（クラスター）をピンポイントで特定して、皮肉っぽい表現や推論プロセスといった反応を直接コントロール（ステアリング）できるようになるんですって！🎯

実験ではモデルによって経路の個性が異なることも分かっています：
・Gemma 4 31b：同じ経路を使い回すことが多く、安定した動きを見せます。🔄
・Gemma 4 26b：プロンプトごとにバラバラな経路を辿り、まるで毛糸玉のように複雑怪奇！🧶
・Qwen 3.6 35b：その中間くらいの適度な多様性。⚖️

現在は可視化データのサイズが大きすぎて表示が重くなるなどの課題もありますが、将来的には再学習をせずに特定の能力を「外科手術」のように微調整できる技術基盤になりそうです。モデルの高度なカスタマイズを目指す人にとって、これは目が離せない研究領域ですね！🚀

title: Refugees, asylum seekers being arrested and deported in Egypt: report
content: Egypt has been arbitrarily arresting and deporting refugees with expired permits, Human Rights Watch (HRW) reported Tuesday. The majority of these refugees and asylum seekers are from Sudan and South Sudan. Sudan is in year four of a deadly civil war, while renewed violence plagues South Sudan . The situation in Egypt is due in part to a legal quagmire. In 2024, the government passed an asylum law that is supposed to transfer asylum duties to the government from the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), but the transfer has not taken place. There is now a backlog for both the government and UNHCR, and people with expired permits are “given renewal dates as late as 2028.” Per Human Rights Watch, the arrests are occurring because of these delays. Egyptian authorities have reportedly arrested thousands of refugees this year. Furthermore, the new law does not contain the principle of non-refoulement , which means countries shall not return migrants to a country where “they would face torture, cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment and other irreparable harm.” Non-refoulement applies regardless of immigration status. As party to the 1951 Refugee Convention , Egypt must comply. Also enshrined in the Convention are due process requirements. Article 32 states expulsion can only occur with due process of law. Article 16 states that refugees should have full access to courts that nationals have. Additionally, Article 31 states that countries shall not impose penalties on those fleeing situations that threaten life or freedom. Egypt is home to over a million refugees. It passed the 2024 law to control illegal immigration and smuggling networks. The law also came when European countries had refugee problems of their own and migration was surging because of global conflicts. content: A coalition of 22 Democratic state attorneys general filed a comment letter Monday opposing the Trump administration’s proposed tariffs of up to 12.5 percent on 59 countries and the EU, arguing they are unlawful and amount to a pretext to reimpose broad tariffs previously struck down by the courts. The coalition , co-led by California Attorney General Rob Bonta, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes, filed its objections in response to a proposal by the US Trade Representative to impose tariffs under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 on countries the administration says have failed to enforce prohibitions on goods made with forced labor. The targeted 60 economies account for more than 99 percent of all US imports. “After his first two attempts to impose tariffs were declared illegal by the courts, including the US Supreme Court, the President is back at it again,” Bonta said. “Tariffs are taxes, and the American people cannot shoulder extra costs—no matter how much President Trump wants them to.” In the letter , the attorneys general argued that the proposed tariffs bear little connection to the forced labor concerns they are supposed to address and are instead an attempt to revive the sweeping tariffs the Supreme Court struck down in February. They pointed to the speed of the process, completed in roughly two and a half months rather than the year or more that Section 301 investigations typically require, along with the sheer scope of the targeting 60 economies at once, as evidence that the forced labor rationale is a pretext rather than a genuine basis for the tariffs. US Trade Representative Ambassador Jamieson Greer said that the failure of trading partners to address goods made with forced labor was “unacceptable” and that the US would “no longer tolerate this disparity.” The post Democratic AGs oppose Trump administration’s proposed ‘forced labor’
author: Isabella Luciani | U. Pittsburgh School of Law, US

title: Impeachment trial begins for Philippines vice president
content: The impeachment trial of Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte began Monday on charges of bribery, graft and other corruption. Duterte is currently facing four articles of impeachment . The Philippine House of Representatives voted to impeach her in May with 257 votes in favor, with only 106 needed to impeach. Under the Philippines Constitution , the Senate has the sole power to try all impeachment cases. A two-thirds majority is needed to convict. Since Duterte is not president, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the Philippines does not preside. Deciding who is to preside began Monday’s proceedings. Two senators tried to block the election of the presiding officer. They argued the Senate President must preside. However, the House Prosecutors argued that the Senate sets its own rules. The block was unsuccessful. Following that question, opening arguments began . Representative Jinky Luistro delivered the prosecution’s opening statement, calling the case “a story about power exercised without accountability, a story about public trust betrayed, a story about a public office that stopped answering to the public.” She added that “if wealth was lawfully acquired, where was the lawful explanation? If transactions were proper, where is the complete accounting? If numbers truly add up, why do they refuse to reconcile?” Defense attorney Sheila Sison brought up the number of votes Duterte received and accused the House of running a “mini trial” before the case reached the Senate. The defense stated that “justice includes fairness, without fairness there is abuse” A possible conviction means removal from office along with disqualification from running for future offices. Criminal prosecution is possible, but not mandatory. The post Impeachment trial begins for Philippines vice president appeared first on JURIST - News .

title: Google's new remote attestation scheme is every bit as terrible as its old remote attestation scheme
content: Google owes its existence to the open web, but today, its technological “innovations” have much to do with locking users into a “walled garden.” The latest of these is “ reCAPTCHA Mobile Verification ,” an experimental initiative that will let companies block users if they are running independent, "de-googled" versions of Android. These “indie Android” versions are favored by people who want to protect their privacy and their attention by blocking trackers and ads. Worse, this is just the latest in a line of similarly user-hostile measures. Long before “agentic AI,” we had the idea that software would act as your agent on the internet. That's why the old-fashioned technical term for a browser is a “user agent.” Your browser acts on your behalf to retrieve information and then show it to you, in the format you choose. It's your agent . This is a powerful and profound idea. It is because browsers are our “agents” that we expect them to accept our directives, say, by blocking pop-ups, or by turning off autoplay sound, or by blocking commercial surveillance trackers . Your browser does all that because your browser works for you . The reason your browser can work for you is that the web is an open, standardized technology. In theory, anyone who follows the standards published by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) can make a browser, and that web browser can connect to any web server. Browsers and servers are interoperable . It's the same force that means you can put anyone's gas in your gas-tank, or anyone's shoelaces in your shoes, or anyone's milk on your cereal. But what if manufacturers could dictate those choices to you? What if your light socket refused to use a lightbulb unless it was officially blessed by the socket's manufacturer?
